title: One Neighbor's Petition Helped Stop a $5 Billion Data Center
summary:
In Landover, Maryland, nearly 90 acres of empty land stretch out where a shopping mall once stood. Landover Mall closed in 2002, and the site has sat mostly vacant ever since. In 2024, the developer that built the mall won approval to build a $5 billion data center campus there.

A data center is a giant building full of computers that keep the internet running. Data centers use huge amounts of water and electricity, and many run backup generators that burn diesel fuel. Taylor Frazier McCollum lived less than a mile from the site, and she did not want one in her neighborhood. 'Why would you want to bring water-polluting, diesel-generating data centers right down the street from where people live, work, play?' she asked.

McCollum started a petition that gathered more than 25,000 signatures. The petition led to large protests and several local pauses, called moratoriums, on data center projects across the county. The $5 billion project, which was set to break ground between 2026 and 2027, is now blocked. Across the country, community opposition has prompted about 500 such moratoriums on data centers.

The fight changed McCollum's life. She does not own a home. In 2024, she and her young daughter were evicted from their apartment after her wages were cut, and they moved in with her grandfather. She went to county meetings, testified before Maryland lawmakers, and found herself working alongside environmentalists, neighbors worried about electric bills, and people new to organizing.

Not everyone agrees the pause is good news. The county faces a budget deficit, and some worry about lost tax money. Council member Wanika Fisher said the county needs development and a real conversation about its economic future. McCollum now wants a full ban on data center projects and has shared her story with communities in Atlanta, Memphis, and Zambia. She hopes to run for office one day, after she pays off her debts and finds a home.
why_it_matters: This story shows how one neighbor can shape what gets built near homes, and it raises a wider question about balancing clean water, air, and power bills against jobs and tax money from new development.

background_read: A data center is a large building full of computers that store information and keep websites and online services running, and running all those computers takes a great deal of water and electricity.
In Landover, Maryland, a developer wanted to build a large data center campus on land where a shopping mall once stood and had sat mostly empty since the mall closed.

A neighbor, Taylor Frazier McCollum, worried about pollution and the strain on water and power near homes, so she started a petition and joined protests that led local officials to pause data center projects, called moratoriums, while the community debated what should happen next.
